Distal humerus fractures: 2

CT of a distal humerus fracture shows one articular portion separated while the remaining articular surface stays connected to the shaft. Which broad AO category best describes this relationship between the joint surface and diaphysis?

  1. AO type A: extra-articular
  2. AO type C: complete articular
  3. Simple diaphyseal fracture
  4. Segmental shaft fracture
  5. AO type B: partial articular
Answer and explanation

AO type B: partial articular

Part of the articular surface remains connected to the shaft in a partial-articular fracture.

Option explanations

AO type B: partial articular: Part of the articular surface remains connected to the shaft in a partial-articular fracture.

AO type A: extra-articular: The articular surface is not involved in an extra-articular distal humerus fracture. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.

AO type C: complete articular: The articular component is entirely separated from the shaft in a complete-articular fracture. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.

Simple diaphyseal fracture: A shaft fracture without intermediate fragments is distinct from an articular classification. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.

Segmental shaft fracture: Separate fracture levels isolate an intervening segment of the diaphysis. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
